- ~1,100 public MCS points could support current 6,000-20,000 electric trucks; need 8,500-14,000 by 2030 for all-European long-haul
- US truck MCS market: US$116.6 million (2025) → US$1.15 billion (2034), 28.9% CAGR. California (Advanced Clean Trucks rule; 33,000 drayage trucks zero-emission by 2035) leads deployment
- Depot charging (slow AC/DC overnight) accounted for 45.6% of truck MCS market in 2024
- Grid bottleneck: distribution/transmission upgrades are the primary constraint; European automakers group (ACEA) calls for 9x faster deployment of commercial vehicle charging infrastructure by 2030

**TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) Dynamics:**
- IEA: In China, battery-electric heavy trucks already at TCO parity with diesel in many use cases (despite ~3x purchase price) due to ~55% higher efficiency and ~70% lower direct energy costs
- US/EU long-haul TCO parity expected by 2030 (without subsidies); Energy Innovation (2025) projects parity for short-haul tractors and vans by 2027-2028, Class 8 long-haul around 2030 (earlier in low-electricity-cost states like Texas)
- Volvo Trucks and ICCT both conclude BEVs will lead all zero-emission pathways by 2030 (including hydrogen FCEVs, HVO, e-diesel, bio-CNG)
- Capex gap remains: US Class 8 diesel tractor ~US$175,000 vs BEV >US$300,000 (2024); IRA provides up to US$40,000 tax credit; European ZEV truck price premium ~US$60,000 lower than US

**Battery vs. Hydrogen Debate:**
- FCEVs offer 15-20 minute refueling, 700-1,000 km range, up to 4,000 lbs more payload vs 1 MWh battery trucks, weather-independent performance. Pilots: Daimler, Hyundai (Xcient), Nikola (2024-2025)
- Cambridge professor David Cebon: green-hydrogen trucks require ~3x the electricity of equivalent BEVs due to energy losses (electrolysis, compression, transport, fuel cell conversion); FCEV capital costs ~2x BEV
- NACFE takes "parallel" view: BEVs for short-haul/regional; FCEVs reserved for heaviest, longest, payload-constrained routes
- IEA 2025 models: FCEVs remain niche until 2030; BEVs dominate on TCO

**Policy Frameworks:**
- EU: CO₂ reductions of 45% by 2030, 65% by 2035, 90% by 2040 for HDVs (Reg. 2019/1242, revised May 2024; €4,250 fine per 1g CO₂ over standard from 2025); urban buses 100% ZEV by 2035 (90% interim 2030); March 2026 flexibility arrangements passed for 2025-2029
- US: EPA Phase 3 GHG standards finalized March 2024 (up to 60% CO₂ reduction for vocational trucks, 40% for tractors by 2032), under reconsideration by Trump administration (mid-2025); CARB continues enforcement in California
- China: NEV purchase tax exemption extended to end-2025 (full), 50% through 2027; truck scrappage subsidies extended to 2025; stricter diesel truck emission standards from July 2023. Electric truck sales doubled 2023→2024; single Hebei province >30,000 electric truck sales
- UK: VETS scheme requires 22% BEV/FCEV van sales by 2024 rising annually
- India: 2030 targets - 70% EV commercial vehicle sales, 800,000 diesel bus replacement; PM E-DRIVE (₹10,900 crore/US$1.28B) drove 1.13 million EVs in first year; e-commercial vehicle sales grew 120% YoY in 2024
- Global ZEV MOU: 100% ZEV buses/trucks by 2040 (30% by 2030); 27+ national governments signed

**OEM Landscape:**
- BYD holds 20%+ of global electric commercial vehicle market (2025); top 5 (BYD, Ford, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, Yutong) = 43% combined
- European OEM strategies: Volvo (broad coverage, early mover), Daimler (long-haul with eActros 600 + own MCS network), Scania/MAN/Renault (regional, urban, parcel delivery)
- Tesla Semi full production at Nevada Gigafactory from 2026; Pepsi, Frito-Lay, Saia each accumulated millions of test miles
- Fleet customers: Amazon operates 20,000+ Rivian EDVs (target 100,000 by 2030); DB Schenker to deploy 100+ MAN eTGX by 2026; Climate United (US nonprofit) announced US$250 million investment over 3 years in zero-emission heavy trucks (Oct 2024) - largest US ZEV truck order, leased to California port drayage operators

**Remaining Challenges:**
- Capex gap and residual value uncertainty (no liquid secondhand market for e-trucks yet); battery-as-a-service and energy-as-a-service models emerging
- Grid readiness: transformer/substation permits take 24-48 months; ACEA calls for 9x faster infrastructure deployment by 2030
- Payload/range: Daimler e-trucks 1,400-1,800 kg heavier than diesel; 1 MWh battery loses 4,000-20,000 lbs payload; cell energy density improving 5-7% annually; solid-state not cost-competitive for trucks until early 2030s
- Cold weather: arXiv 2025 study shows significant range loss and slower charging at 25°F to -25°F; mitigation (heated battery swapping, pre-conditioning, hybrid depot/corridor architectures) becoming standard in Nordic/Canadian/US northern fleets

**Future Outlook:**
- IEA projects >5 million barrels/day oil demand reduction by 2030 from global road transport electrification
- Electrification is not one curve but several: city buses approach saturation in Europe/China by 2030; last-mile vans next; regional/short-haul tractors cross TCO parity late 2020s; Class 8 long-haul mainstream affordability early 2030s; some long-haul high-payload applications may remain hydrogen FCEV into the 2040s
- Where policy and infrastructure are coordinated (China, EU, California), electrification advances rapidly; where left to market forces (most of US outside California, much of developing world), penetration remains in single digits
</summary>

The research compares TCO for three truck types (semi-trailer tractors, dump trucks, and cargo trucks) across Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, examining when new energy freight trucks will reach TCO parity with conventional diesel trucks. The study supports China's goal of having new energy vehicles comprise 20% of sales by 2025.

Key findings:
- All battery-electric truck models can reach TCO parity with diesel trucks by 2030
- Electric dump trucks can achieve parity around 2025
- Cargo trucks and semi-trailer tractors achieve parity between 2025-2030
- Hydrogen fuel cell cargo trucks and dump trucks only reach approximate cost parity with diesel around 2030

The paper offers four policy recommendations for China:

Set aggressive short-term sales requirements for new energy heavy-duty vehicles (citing California as a model, which requires 11% zero-emission heavy truck sales by 2025 and 50% by 2030; for zero-emission semi-trailer tractors: 5% by 2025 and 30% by 2030). 2. Set long-term new energy vehicle sales targets to provide manufacturers with a clear blueprint for product design and investment, combining short-term binding sales requirements with long-term non-binding goals.
3. Provide incentive policies during 2020-2025 to close the TCO gap between new energy and diesel heavy-duty trucks, following the "polluter pays" principle to fund long-term incentive programs, with limited subsidy scope and duration.
4. Develop targeted but technology-neutral policies that favor trucks with highest CO2 emissions (like semi-trailer tractors) while creating a fair competitive environment for both battery-electric and fuel cell trucks. --- SOURCE 8: Battery Cost per kWh in 2026: What Drives It | BatteryMBA ---
URL: https://www.battery.mba/resources/battery-cost-per-kwh

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from BatteryMBA examines what drives battery cost per kWh, arguing that quoting a single battery cost figure is meaningless without four qualifiers: segment, chemistry, region, and whether the number refers to a cell, pack, or installed system.

**Key pricing data (BloombergNEF, December 2025 survey):**
- Global volume-weighted average pack price: $108/kWh in 2025, down 8% from 2024 (record low)
- Battery electric vehicle packs: $99/kWh (up slightly from $97 nominal in 2024, second year below $100)
- Stationary storage packs: $70/kWh, down 45% in a single year — cheapest segment for the first time
- Global average cell price (all segments): $74/kWh, down 5%
- LFP packs: $81/kWh average vs. NMC packs at $128/kWh (lowest observed LFP pack at $50, lowest cell at $36)
- Regional spread: China $84/kWh; North America $121 (44% higher); Europe $131 (56% higher)

**Cost composition of cells:** Materials (largest block, dominated by cathode active material, often a third+ of total cell cost for nickel chemistries), depreciation (spread across production volume, making utilization critical), yield loss (scrapped cells carry full accumulated cost), energy (drying and dry room), labor, and overheads/warranty/margin (compressed to thin or negative margins due to overcapacity). Pack integration adds module hardware, BMS, wiring, thermal management, enclosure, and assembly.

**2026 market disruption:** Battery-grade lithium carbonate bottomed at ~$8,000/tonne in mid-2025 then rebounded sharply, trading between ~150,000-181,500 yuan/tonne ($21,000-25,500) in H1 2026. IEA's Global EV Outlook 2026 noted lithium prices at start of 2026 were more than double a year earlier, still ~70% below the 2022 peak. Pack prices did not rise in step due to long-term contracts, hedging, LFP migration, and margin compression — China held ~557 GWh of annual stationary storage cell capacity (roughly double global demand). BloombergNEF still forecast a further decline to just under $105/kWh for 2026 (~3% drop), but this assumption of never-passing-through input costs is identified as the key forecast vulnerability.

**System cost insight:** At $70/kWh for stationary storage packs, batteries are no longer the dominant cost in installed grid storage projects. The levers for project economics now shift to interconnection queues, construction efficiency, cost of capital, and revenue stacking — a general pattern when one component falls by an order of magnitude.

**Guidance for using cost numbers:** Always state the boundary (cell/pack/installed system), segment, chemistry, region, year, and whether nominal or real; distinguish price from cost (survey prices can sit below production cost during price wars); and check data freshness (18-month-old figures belong in history charts, not models).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Quoting a single battery cost per kWh is close to meaningless without four qualifiers: which segment, which chemistry, which region, and whether the number is a cell, a pack or an installed system. The spread across those four is larger than the year-on-year change that usually makes the headlines."
</key_excerpts>

## Solid-State Battery Mass Production Countdown: Toyota, CATL, BYD's Three Paths

This article from TMTPost (published 2026.06.22) examines the 2026 solid-state battery mass production race among the three major players: Toyota, CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology), and BYD. The key distinction is between **semi-solid-state** batteries (retaining 5%-20% liquid electrolyte) which are the current production mainstream, and **full solid-state** batteries (zero liquid electrolyte) which represent the true endgame solution.

### The Core Problem: Range Anxiety
- Current mainstream EVs have CLTC ranges of 400-700 km with 800V platforms and 5C fast charging (10% to 80% in 30 min), but a Beijing-to-Shanghai trip (~1,200 km) still requires two charging stops.
- Solid-state batteries achieve 400-500 Wh/kg energy density, 1.5-2x current lithium batteries (150-300 Wh/kg), potentially enabling 1,000+ km single-charge range.

### The Three Routes

**Toyota (Sulfide Route – hardest, highest ceiling):**
- Over a decade of R&D, cumulative investment exceeding one trillion yen.
- Sulfide electrolyte has ion conductivity closest to liquid electrolytes; targets 450-500 Wh/kg, 1,200 km range.
- But sulfide materials are sensitive to water and air, making manufacturing extremely difficult.
- Announced in February 2026: postponed full solid-state mass production from 2026 to **2028** due to lower-than-expected EV demand and engineering scaling gaps.
- New timeline: 2028 small-batch installation, debuting on Lexus high-end models.

**CATL (Stepped Approach – most stable):**
- Dual-track strategy: sulfide + condensed polymer routes; most full solid-state patents globally; 1GWh pilot line completed.
- April 2026: launched Kirin condensed-state battery (classified as semi-solid, <10% electrolyte, 350 Wh/kg cell energy density), enabling ~1,500 km range for sedans and 80% charge in 10 minutes.
- Hefei solid-state line first products reached 450 Wh/kg, approaching Toyota's target; 2027 installation with Li Auto (理想汽车) models; 500 Wh/kg next-gen in development targeting 2030 mass production.

**BYD (Latest Entrant – slowest but cost-focused):**
- Chongqing Bishan 20GWh production line expected to break ground in Q3 2026; cell energy density 400 Wh/kg (system up to 480 Wh/kg).
- Passed C-NCAP (中汽研) vehicle certification in April 2026.
- Vehicle installation expected 2027 (Yangwang U9 and Han EV high-end versions); mass adoption after 2030.
- Target: reduce full solid-state cell cost to 0.5-0.7 yuan/Wh by 2030, achieving parity with liquid batteries ("固液同价").

### Current Costs & Buying Advice
- Full solid-state cell cost: 1.6-2.2 yuan/Wh vs. LFP at 0.39-0.5 yuan/Wh (3-5x more expensive). A 70kWh pack costs 80,000+ yuan more.
- Semi-solid costs falling: targeting <1.2 yuan/Wh in 2026; MG4 semi-solid version priced from 99,800 yuan (with subsidy).
- National standard GB/T 43568-2026 (first global vehicle-use solid-state battery standard) takes effect **July 1, 2026**, strictly distinguishing semi vs. full solid-state. No production vehicle currently meets full solid-state standards.
- Advice: Buy semi-solid now if needed (10-300k yuan price range, 600-800 km range); wait for Toyota (2028) or CATL (2027) full solid-state if can wait 2-3 years; full solid-state at LFP prices is a post-2030 story.

### Conclusion
- Semi-solid batteries already deliver 800 km range at the price of previous 600 km liquid batteries.
- Full solid-state endgame awaits BYD bringing down costs.
</summary>

## Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Comparison: Electric Vehicles vs. Internal Combustion Engine Vehicles

This webpage from the Nickel Institute presents findings from comprehensive Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) studies comparing electric vehicles (EVs) with internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles across three major global regions. The research was commissioned by the Nickel Institute and conducted by Avicenne Energy (for Europe) and ZTE (for Asia-Pacific) in 2020-2021.

**Background:** The global EV market is growing due to the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from ICE vehicles. Nickel is a critical component of lithium-ion batteries, which offer the highest energy density, the broadest temperature operating range (from cold northern winters to hot desert conditions), and exceptional cycling capability—allowing EVs to travel a million miles or more before requiring battery replacement.

**Global TCO Study (2021):** The Nickel Institute conducted a detailed TCO investigation across the US (California, New York, Florida), Europe (France, Germany, UK), and Asia (China, Japan, Korea). Vehicles were categorized as small, mid-size, and luxury cars, with at least one EV and one ICE vehicle compared in each category. Metrics examined included purchase cost, subsidies, taxes, charger costs, gasoline prices, electricity rates, maintenance costs, resale value, and annual driving distance. TCO values were calculated for 3-year, 7-year, and 10-year ownership periods under high-mileage and low-mileage scenarios. Manufacturers covered included GM, Tesla, BMW, Volkswagen, Peugeot, Honda, Nissan, Kia, Toyota, Hyundai, and JAC.

**Key Findings:**
- Across all regions, EVs have higher sticker prices than comparable ICE vehicles, sometimes significantly so, but EV subsidies and higher resale values are major offsetting factors in TCO.
- For the vast majority of small and mid-size EVs, owning an EV is financially advantageous across most regions and scenarios.
- Gasoline/diesel costs being higher than electricity costs in Europe and Asia significantly impacts TCO in those regions.
- Luxury EVs have a starkly different picture: purchase prices can be nearly double those of comparable ICE vehicles (e.g., Tesla S at €81,990 vs. BMW 5 Series at €47,700 in Europe). This price gap offsets high oil costs, meaning luxury EVs may have higher TCO than ICE vehicles for high-mileage drivers.
- The US has the lowest gasoline prices and fewest subsidies, making EV TCO less favorable there, though results may shift over time as EV costs decline.
- Europe accounts for 15% of global light vehicle sales but 43% of global BEV/PHEV sales (2020, up 140% from 2019), while the US accounts for ~20% of auto sales but only 10% of global EV/PHEV sales.
- European electricity costs are 1.4 to 3.3 times higher than in the US; European gasoline costs are 1.5 to 2.8 times higher than in the US.
- Germany has the highest electricity costs and lowest gasoline prices in Europe, making EV TCO closest to ICE there.
- In China (largest EV market—1.34 million EV sales in 2020), electricity costs are very low, purchase cost differences between EV and ICE are small, and public charging infrastructure is excellent with over 1 million charging points (vs. 40,000 in Japan and 30,000 in Korea). - Public charger electricity rates are typically double home charging rates, so public charging should be minimized.
- In Japan and Korea, EV purchase costs can be more than double equivalent ICE vehicles due to limited supply, but this gap is expected to narrow when domestic OEMs launch vehicles in 2022-2023.
- In Asia, subsidies can cover up to 20% of the purchase price. In China, license plates are obtained only through auction, costing over 50,000 RMB in 2020.
- Misconceptions about EV range limitations and lack of public charging stations remain barriers to adoption, but evidence clearly shows EVs are more economical for most potential buyers worldwide.

Subsidies, taxes, and incentives vary significantly across EU countries, sometimes accounting for up to 20% of purchase price. Luxury EV TCO only outperforms ICE in the short term (3 years) because ICE vehicles lose more value early in ownership.

## China New Energy Vehicle (NEV) Motor & Electronic Control Industry Analysis (2026)

This webpage from 智研咨询 (China's leading industry consulting firm) provides a comprehensive analysis of China's new energy vehicle (NEV) motor and electronic control industry, covering definitions, market status, industrial chain, policies, competitive landscape, and development trends.

### Industry Definition
- NEVs differ from traditional vehicles through the "Three Electric" systems: electric drive, battery, and electronic control
- Electric drive consists of transmission mechanisms, motors, and inverters
- Motors comprise stator, rotor, and housing; the rotor is the main drive motor
- Motor and electronic control systems replace traditional engines/transmissions and directly determine EV performance in climbing, acceleration, and top speed

### Market Status & Key Data
- In 2025, China's automotive production and sales both exceeded 34 million units, setting new records
- From January to April 2026, China's NEV production and sales reached 4.285 million and 4.304 million units respectively (production down 3.2% YoY, sales up 0.1% YoY)
- Mainstream NEVs typically use 1-2 sets of motors and controllers
- **2025 demand**: Approximately 24.735 million sets of NEV motors and controllers, with a market size of ~272.085 billion yuan
- **Jan-Apr 2026 demand**: Approximately 6.456 million sets, with a market size of ~71.016 billion yuan
- Average unit price calculated at 11,000 yuan per set
- Industry relies heavily on NEV market prosperity and is expected to maintain rapid growth

### Industrial Chain
- **Upstream**: Permanent magnet materials (NdFeB), electrical steel (silicon steel sheets), power semiconductors, precision bearings, sensors
- **Midstream**: Motor and electronic control manufacturing (high technical barriers)
- **Downstream**: NEV manufacturers and aftermarket services

### Competitive Landscape
Two main market participant groups:
1. **Traditional automakers with in-house R&D**: BYD, BAIC, Xiamen King Long
2. **Professional third-party suppliers**: Bosch, Continental, Shanghai Edrive, Broad-Ocean Motor, Inovance Technology, INVT

**Key company highlights**:
- **BYD**: 2025 revenue of 803.965 billion yuan, with transportation equipment and electrical manufacturing revenue of 648.646 billion yuan (79.45% of total). Master of full NEV industry chain core technologies
- **Wolong Electric Drive**: Global leader in motor and drive products; 2025 production of 557,000 units of NEV transportation electric drive systems, sales of 511,000 units, revenue of 433 million yuan

### Development Trends
1. **Integration & High Voltage**: Shift from dispersed components to "multi-in-one" integrated systems (3-in-1 to 8-in-1); 800V high-voltage platforms with SiC power modules enabling charging speeds like 400km range in 10 minutes
2. **Efficiency & Lightweight**: Flat wire motors, oil cooling, high-speed motors (20000rpm+), power density exceeding 6.5kW/kg; carbon fiber rotor retainers and topology optimization for weight reduction
3. **Intelligence & Connectivity**: Motors evolving into "smart power brains" with AI, IoT, big data integration, OTA upgrades, and fault self-diagnosis
4. **Globalization**: Shifting from domestic competition to global ecosystem collaboration; "dual-super + multi-strong + specialized" market structure; Chinese companies expanding to Europe and Southeast Asia, transitioning from manufacturing output to technology and standard output

--- SOURCE 1: 电车电池健康度自测指南 你的电池还剩多少寿命？_车生活-汽车之家论坛 ---
URL: https://club.m.autohome.com.cn/bbs/thread/ec6740a8db4e9c95/115919420-1.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a comprehensive guide (in Chinese) for EV battery health self-assessment, published on Automotive (汽车之家) on 2026-08-24. The article teaches EV owners how to evaluate battery lifespan without disassembling the vehicle, focusing on two key metrics: SOH (State of Health) and cell voltage differential (电芯压差).

**Key Metrics:**
- SOH = current actual capacity ÷ rated factory capacity. SOH ≥90% = excellent (7-8 yrs remaining); 85-90% = good (5-7 yrs); 80-85% = aging begins; 70-80% = significant decay, consider replacement; <70% = severe aging, immediate replacement advised. Industry treats 80% as the threshold for battery "second life" (repurposing to energy storage stations).
- Cell voltage differential is more critical than SOH: ≤0.05V is normal; 0.05–0.1V requires monitoring; >0.1V means severe consistency degradation and high risk of sudden power failure, making the car dangerous even if SOH appears normal.

**Three Self-Testing Methods:**
1. Charge-volume reverse calculation (free): Discharge to 20%, fast-charge to 100%, record kWh charged, then actual capacity ≈ charged kWh ÷ 0.8 ÷ 0.92. Divide by rated capacity to get SOH. This exposes dealer "flashed" fake SOH readings.
2. Vehicle system/APP direct check (available on BYD, Tesla, NIO, XPeng, Li Auto, etc.), but caveat: SOH and cycle counts can be altered for ~50 yuan, so never rely on it alone.
3. 4S dealer diagnostic tool (most authoritative, essential for used car purchases): Reads true SOH, cycle count, fast-charge ratio, per-cell voltage/internal resistance differentials, and fault history. Produces a printed battery inspection report.

**National Standards (2026):**
- New national standard GB/T 46991.1-2025 (effective 2026-07-01) requires battery capacity retention: ≥82% at 5 years/100,000 km; ≥75% at 8 years/160,000 km; ≥70% at 10 years/200,000 km. Onboard display error vs. actual measurement must not exceed 5%.
- Power battery testing is now mandatory in annual vehicle inspections; SOH below thresholds fails inspection.

**Battery Replacement Pricing (effective 2026-04-01):**
- New national maximum price caps: LFP (lithium iron phosphate) batteries at 150 yuan/kWh (50-kWh car = 7,500 yuan full pack; 70-kWh = 10,500 yuan); ternary lithium at 180 yuan/kWh (50-kWh = 9,000 yuan; 70-kWh = 12,600 yuan).
- "Repair don't replace" is now mandatory. ~75% of battery faults are localized: single cell repair costs 300–800 yuan; module repair 2,000–5,000 yuan (only 10-30% of full replacement cost).
- Old battery residual value belongs to owner: ternary lithium recycling pays 550–650 yuan/kWh; a 50-kWh old battery can offset 17,500–22,500 yuan, potentially making replacement nearly free.

**Warranty Terms by Brand:**
- BYD: 8yr/150,000km (first owner lifetime), free replacement below 70% SOH (65% for flagship models)
- Tesla: 8yr/160,000–192,000km, below 70% capacity
- NIO: first-owner lifetime warranty, below 80% health (flexible battery-swap system)
- XPeng: 8yr/150,000km, >10% decay in 2 yrs / >15% in 4 yrs / >20% in 8 yrs
- Li Auto: 8yr/150,000km, >10% in 2yrs / >15% in 5yrs / >20% in 8yrs
- GAC Toyota Platinum: 8yr/150,000km, >10% in 2yrs / >20% in 6yrs / >25% in 8yrs
- Most warranties are 8 years or 150,000 km (whichever first), first-owner only, require full 4S service history.

**Battery-Destroying Habits:**
1. Parking long-term at 100% charge (biggest killer)
2. Frequent high-current fast charging
3. Deep discharge below 10%
4. Charging in extreme heat/cold
5. Parking long-term without battery state management (recommend 40-60% charge in cool conditions)

Maintenance tip: Keep charge between 20-80%, minimize fast charging, avoid prolonged sun exposure—can extend battery life by ~30%.

**FAQ Highlights:**
- One full cycle = 0% to 100%. Home cars do only 100-150 full cycles/year. LFP rated ≥2,000 cycles; ternary lithium ≥1,200 cycles.
- Used cars with SOH <80% are not recommended for purchase (less than 3 years of life left; winter range only 65-70% of new).
- Under 2026 regulations, if decay exceeds 20% (SOH below 80%), manufacturers must replace the battery pack free of charge unconditionally; third-party test reports have legal validity.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"看电池寿命，就看一个数——SOH（健康度），以及一个比 SOH 更关键的隐藏指标电芯压差。SOH 80% 以上放心开，低于 70% 就是该换电池的红线。而电芯压差一旦超过 0.1V，即便 SOH 显示正常，也可能随时趴窝。"

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from OFweek (a Chinese technology news platform) analyzes the development status and prospects of in-wheel motor (轮毂电机) technology for new energy vehicles (NEVs), using patent data from the PatSnap global patent database.

**Key Market Context:**
- The global NEV drive motor market reached 16.2 billion RMB in 2020 and is projected to reach 48.8 billion RMB by 2026, with a CAGR of 17.1%.
- In-wheel motor technology is considered by industry experts as the ultimate solution for new energy and intelligent connected vehicle powertrains, offering advantages such as simplified structure, energy efficiency improvements of 8-15%, extended vehicle range, and independently controllable drive/brake torque. However, drawbacks include increased unsprung mass, high waterproof/dustproof/vibration requirements, and heat dissipation challenges.

**Technology Types and Representatives:**
1. **High-speed inner rotor motors** — Represented by Germany's Schaeffler (patent WO2020181466A1, "Hub motor driving system and motor vehicle," filed 2019). Schaeffler's design optimizes lubricant storage through repositioning of radial bearings and seals. Schaeffler has started mass production and has tested on vehicles including the Schaeffler Mover, German Aerospace Center's U-Shift, and Innvelo 48V fuel cell concept vehicle.
2. **Low-speed outer rotor motors** — Represented by UK's Protean (patent GB2456351A, "Vehicle with in-wheel motor brake," filed 2008). This design can deliver braking power exceeding 200kW, decelerating a ~1.5-ton vehicle from 60 mph in 5 seconds, while the motor weighs only ~30kg.

**Patent Analysis Findings:**
- Annual patent applications for in-wheel motors are rising significantly, divided into three phases: pre-2010 (avg ~150/year, high approval rate), 2011-2015 (avg ~560/year), and 2016-present (avg ~1,500/year). PatSnap projects growth to 1,793 in 2021, 2,328 in 2022, and 2,525 in 2023.
- **China** is the most targeted market for in-wheel motor patents, followed by Japan and the US. Within China, Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces lead in patent filings, followed by Guangdong and Beijing.
- **Japanese companies** hold 61.4% of in-wheel motor patents, with NTN Corporation alone accounting for over 39.3%. Japanese firms (NTN, Toyota, Nissan) have the strongest technical capabilities. In contrast, Chinese domestic patent filings come primarily from universities, with insufficient corporate patent reserves.
- High-value patents cluster around vehicle stability control, yaw rate, electric wheel vehicle models, and yaw moment — indicating market emphasis on stability and handling impacts.

**Industry History:**
- The technology dates to 1950 when American Robert invented an integrated hub device combining motor, transmission, and braking. General Motors applied it to large mining trucks in 1968.
- Japan first used the technology in 1991, General Motors in 2003, and France's Michelin in 2007.
- Chinese companies are advancing through acquisitions and independent R&D — e.g., Evergrande Group fully acquired UK's Protean; GAC Group launched NEV models GE3, GS4 PHEV, GA3S PHEV.

**Conclusion:**
China's in-wheel motor development remains immature with limited application, requiring international cooperation to catch up with advanced global levels. The technology is still in a growth/ascending phase and could drive transformative industry development in NEVs if mass production is achieved.
</summary>

It examines China's rise in the electric motor industry and the debate between centralized vs. distributed drive architectures.

Key points covered:

1. **BYD's Yi Si Fang technology**: China's first mass-produced four-motor independent drive architecture using vector control for dynamic four-wheel control. It works on both pure EV and hybrid platforms and enables capabilities like lateral movement, in-place turns, and amphibious operation. The system is 100% self-developed, including front/rear dual motor assemblies, central controller, and blade battery.

2. **Motor industry response**: The announcement triggered stock rallies in Chinese motor companies including Tongda Power (002576, hit limit-up), Fangzheng Motor (002196), and Wolong Electric Drive (600580).

3. **Rivian precedent**: BYD's wheel-side motor technology was preceded by US startup Rivian, whose R1T pickup and R1S SUV have used wheel-side motors since 2019, with deliveries starting 2021-2022. Rivian's vehicles also feature in-place turning and ~1 meter wading depth.

4. **China's motor industry rise**: China's motor sector was historically at the bottom of the global value chain (Western giants ABB, Siemens controlled large industrial motors; Japan dominated small motors). By 2020, Chinese companies including BYD, Fangzheng Motor, Weiran Power, Ningbo Shuanglin, and Jingjin Power ranked among global top 10 in NEV drive motor installations. CICC estimates the electric drive system market opportunity exceeds 1 trillion RMB.

5. **Why China overtook**: Two key factors: (a) China mastered permanent magnet synchronous motor technology, with near-monopoly control of neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) rare earth raw materials; (b) flat-wire (扁线) motor technology, where China now holds most global flat-wire processing capacity. Tesla's shift to permanent magnet motors and Chinese suppliers in 2018-2021 (including Zhongke Sanhuan and Jinli Yongci entering Tesla's supply chain) accelerated this.

6. **Wheel-side vs. hub motors**: Both are distributed drive forms. Hub motors (putting motors directly in wheel hubs) can improve efficiency 8-15% but face challenges with unsprung mass, waterproofing/dust sealing, and cost. Wheel-side motors (mounted beside wheels) occupy less space and integrate water cooling and reducers. Analysis estimates ~3 trillion RMB market for wheel-side motors at 10% penetration across 1.5 billion global vehicles (4 motors @ 5,000 RMB each = 20,000 RMB/vehicle).

7. **Electric vs. mechanical AWD**: Electric four-wheel drive with software-based torque control has neutralized advantages of mechanical systems like Audi Quattro. However, in extreme off-road conditions where only one wheel has traction, mechanical systems with differential locks can still outperform electric systems.

8. **Concerns**: Reliability and durability questions remain for Yi Si Fang, particularly wheel hard-locking, motor overheating prevention, optimal dynamic adjustment, and backup solutions for sensor/control failures. The article concludes BYD deserves time as the first Chinese automaker to mass-produce four-motor independent drive, quoting a Wang Chuanfu saying about perseverance: "There is no mountain higher than people, no road longer than feet—as long as the soul is not bent, a broad road will be walked out."

SUMMARY:

This webpage is an academic article (editorial/invited paper) published in *Science and Technology Review* (科技导报) in 2020, written by Wang Zhenpo (王震坡) and colleagues from Beijing Institute of Technology, Tongji University, Shanghai University, and Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics. The article is based on the 390th Young Scientists Forum of the China Association for Science and Technology on "Distributed Drive Electric Vehicle Key Technologies and Industrialization Prospects," held in Beijing on November 29–30, 2019.

The paper discusses distributed drive electric vehicles (DDEV), which use in-wheel or wheel-side motors installed inside or near the wheel rim. These vehicles offer flexible body layout, compact structure, modular chassis design, independently controllable wheel drive/braking torques, high maneuverability, and high reliability—making them ideal carriers for future intelligent connected vehicles. However, the technology remains at the laboratory research stage with four key technical challenges:

1) **New distributed drive chassis and adaptive suspension systems**: In-wheel motors significantly increase unsprung mass, reducing ride comfort. New chassis configurations and adaptive suspension systems compatible with x-by-wire subsystems (drive-by-wire, steer-by-wire, brake-by-wire) are needed.

2) **High-efficiency, high-torque-density, high-reliability in-wheel/wheel-side drive systems**: Due to limited installation space and harsh operating conditions, integrated design methods combining motor, motor controller, and braking systems are needed, along with efficient high-precision torque control methods. This involves multi-physics field simulation and innovation in motor structure and manufacturing processes.

3) **High-efficiency, high-safety vehicle control technology**: DDEVs are constrained, over-actuated, statically indeterminate systems with nonlinear, strongly coupled tire forces across longitudinal-lateral-vertical directions. Improving state/parameter estimation accuracy and robustness using in-wheel motor feedback information (torque and speed) under complex conditions is a key issue. Motor-based active control strategies enable per-wheel torque control, all-wheel regenerative braking, traction control, active steering, and direct yaw moment control.

4) **X-by-wire chassis coordinated control technology**: Full x-by-wire chassis integrates drive-by-wire, brake-by-wire, and steer-by-wire subsystems with high control freedom, but subsystem coupling and interaction require decoupling control based on vehicle nonlinear dynamics, along with fault-tolerant control for sensors and key components.

The article also notes from the editor that this paper represents the judgments of the forum chair and five executive chairs on the key technologies and industrialization trends of distributed drive electric vehicles. <summary>
This is a deep industry research report from Chuancai Securities (dated May 24, 2018) covering the lithium battery recycling industry in China. The report provides an "Overweight" (增持) rating and covers the industry for the first time with a long-term bullish outlook.

**Core Thesis:**
- Lithium battery recycling is divided into two streams: cascade utilization (梯次利用) for power batteries and material regeneration for consumer batteries. Retired lithium batteries contain electrolytes and various metals (Li, Co, Cu, Ni, Al, Fe) with economic value, while also posing environmental hazards if improperly disposed.
- Power batteries entered a concentrated retirement period starting 2018, with cascade utilization focused on energy storage applications. 2014 was the "development year" for power batteries; production grew ~10x over three years to 44.5 GWh by 2017. Power battery retirement cycles are about 5 years, so the recycling market enters high growth after 2018. Over the next 3 years, retired batteries will be primarily LFP (lithium iron phosphate), mainly used in energy storage markets. Tower base stations (铁塔基站) are a good application scenario—retired batteries can still achieve 800+ cycle life in energy storage during the 80%-40% capacity decay phase.
- Rising lithium and cobalt prices support the economics of metal regeneration for consumer batteries. Net profit per ton: LFP batteries = -292 yuan, NCM 523 ternary batteries = 17,733 yuan, LCO consumer cobalt acid batteries = 38,729 yuan.

**Market Size:** China's 3C lithium battery output exceeds 50 GWh annually. Power battery output grew from ~4 GWh (2014) to 44 GWh (2017). NEV sales: 1.8 (2013), 7.5 (2014), 33.1 (2015), 50.7 (2016), 77.7 (2017) units—over 100% CAGR. 2020 projection: 2 million NEV sales with 80+ GWh battery demand; LMC Automotive predicts 7 million NEV sales in China by 2025, with battery output exceeding 200 GWh. Battery scrap volume estimated at ~30 GWh in 2018, rising to ~150 GWh by 2025.

**Environmental/Regulatory Drivers:** Batteries contain hazardous materials (Ni, Co, phosphides score over 1000 on CERCLA ecotoxicity). Recycling needs driven by both environmental necessity and economics (energy savings: Al, Ni, Fe regeneration uses significantly less energy than virgin smelting). The EU requires member states to achieve 45% battery collection rates by September 2016 and average effective mass recovery rates of at least 50%.

**Policy Landscape (2006-2017):** A series of national policies established OEM (vehicle manufacturers) as the responsible entity for battery recycling, including the "Production Responsibility Extension System" (生产者责任延伸制度). Key policies include the 2012 State Council plan, the 2016 battery recycling policy, and the 2017 GB/T 34014-2017 automotive power battery coding regulation requiring traceability. National standards include: 余能检测 (residual energy testing, GB/T 34015-2017), 拆解规范 (disassembly specification, GB/T 33598-2017), and 编码规则 (coding rules, GB/T 34014-2017).

**Cascade Utilization:** Power batteries retire from vehicles at ~80% effective capacity, then are used at 80%-40% decay for lower-demand applications; below 40% they enter material regeneration. Process: disassembly → remaining life prediction → system integration → reuse. International case studies in Japan, US, Germany, and China show storage is the best cascade application scenario, covering mobile power, commercial/household storage, grid storage, and smart grid construction. Retired LFP batteries outperform lead-acid batteries in energy density, cycle life (close to 1000 cycles vs. 100 for lead-acid at 100% DOD), and operating temperature.

**Material Regeneration Methods:** International practice (e.g., Umicore) uses pyrometallurgy + hydrometallurgy (smelting at ~1000°C, advantages: handles multiple battery types, high automation; disadvantages: Mn and Li recovery rates low). Chinese companies primarily use hydrometallurgy (discharge, dismantle, dissolve PVDF with NMP, recover Cu/Al foils, acid-base precipitation to separate Co/Li). Advantages: nearly all elements recoverable, 95%+ recovery for Co/Ni, 90%+ for Al/Cu, 75%+ for Li; disadvantages: labor-intensive disassembly due to non-standardized batteries, only handles lithium batteries.

**Economics:** Based on hydrometallurgical routes with assumptions (acquisition cost at 50% of Li/Co value, March 2018 prices, 15% high-tech enterprise tax rate, 6000t plant with 120 million yuan investment, 10-year depreciation): LFP regeneration yields -292 yuan/t net profit, NCM 523 yields 17,733 yuan/t, LCO yields 38,729 yuan/t. LCO has the highest Co content (~178 kg/t) making it most economically attractive.

**Related Companies:** 格林美 (GEM, 002340), 厦门钨业 (Xiamen Tungsten, 600549), 宁德时代 (CATL, 300750), 天奇股份 (Tianqi, 002009), plus recycling leaders 豪鹏, 邦普, 深圳乾泰.

**Risks:** Policy and standard enforcement weaker than expected; significant declines in raw material (Li/Co) prices undermining recycling economics.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
On July 30, 2026, China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) issued Announcement No. 20, officially abolishing the "cascade utilization" (梯次利用) policy for retired electric vehicle power batteries. The announcement ends the administrative management of cascade utilization companies, removing all 100 previously designated "cascade utilization" enterprises from the compliance list, including major lithium battery players such as BYD (SZ: 002594), Huayou Cobalt (SH: 603799), SVOLT (蜂巢能源), and Guoxuan High-Tech (SZ: 002074).

**Background/History of "Cascade Utilization" (2012-2026):**
- 2012: The State Council first proposed encouraging power battery cascade utilization in the "Energy-Saving and New Energy Vehicle Industry Development Plan (2012-2020)."
- August 2019: BAK Battery and China Southern Power Grid's integrated energy company built and operated the first battery-pack-level cascade utilization energy storage project in China (a 15-year planned operation campus project using retired ternary batteries).
- 2020: The Jiangsu Kunshan 208MWh grid-side energy storage station — then the world's largest — was completed, also the largest cascade utilization storage project in China.
- June 2022: The National Energy Administration issued a draft document requiring that large and medium electrochemical energy storage stations "shall not use ternary lithium batteries or sodium-sulfur batteries, and should not use cascade utilization power batteries" — marking the beginning of policy tightening.
- July 2026: Announcement No. 20 completely abolishes cascade utilization policies, ending its application in large-scale energy storage.

**Why Cascade Utilization Was Abandoned (3 core reasons):**
1. **Quality/consistency issues**: Retired batteries have highly inconsistent levels of aging, internal resistance, and self-discharge rates due to varied usage conditions during vehicle service. When grouped into storage systems, severely aged cells cause voltage imbalance, accelerated decay, overheating, and potential thermal runaway/fire risks. Grid-side and large commercial/industrial storage projects have excluded cascade batteries from bidding lists due to safety compliance concerns.
2. **Price advantage eliminated**: From 2020-2022, cascade batteries cost at least 30% less than new cells due to high lithium carbonate prices. But as lithium prices fell and manufacturing scaled up, the cost difference between cascade batteries (after dismantling, testing, sorting, PACK reassembly, and traceability verification) and new energy storage cells has nearly disappeared.
3. **Poor full-lifecycle economics**: Cascade batteries have shorter calendar life and only 1/3 to 1/2 of the remaining effective cycles of new batteries. While initial costs are lower, hidden costs from replacement, maintenance, and fault handling are high. New cells can guarantee 10 years of stable operation, making them more economical on a per-cycle basis.

**Shift Toward Battery Recycling:**
With cascade utilization ended, "recycling utilization" becomes the only pathway for retired batteries, focusing on recovering high-value metals (lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese, copper). On April 1, 2026, a new regulation ("Management Measures for Recycling and Comprehensive Utilization of Waste Power Batteries from New Energy Vehicles") took effect, jointly issued by MIIT and five other departments. It mandates that power battery manufacturers and NEV manufacturers bear recycling responsibility for their batteries and must hand over retired batteries to legally established comprehensive utilization enterprises.

**Industry Response:**
- Battery recycling is expected to enter a new era with large-scale enterprises and a much larger industry scale than cascade utilization ever achieved.
- CATL (SZ: 300750) announced in January 2023 that its subsidiary Brunp (广东邦普) would invest 23.8 billion yuan to build a 500,000-tonne waste battery material recycling project in Foshan. In its H1 2026 semi-annual report (disclosed July 24, 2026), CATL's "battery materials & recycling and mineral resources" business generated 18.811 billion yuan in revenue (up 67.23% year-over-year), the fastest-growing segment among its three main businesses, with a gross margin of 27.04% (up 5.81 percentage points) — the only segment showing margin improvement.

URL: http://www.gast-auto.com/insightDe_91.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from GAST (盖斯特) Strategy Consulting, a Chinese automotive industry consulting firm. The page features an in-depth industry insight article from July 2021 titled "动力电池回收利用关键问题辨析" (Analysis of Key Issues in Power Battery Recycling and Reuse).

**Core Content:**
The article examines the strategic value, challenges, and business models of power battery recycling and reuse in China's new energy vehicle (NEV) industry, addressing ten key questions:

1. **Drivers for battery recycling**: Policy requirements (including China's Extended Producer Responsibility system and regulations on NEV battery recycling traceability), EV cost reduction needs, and economic benefits drive participation. Battery costs account for ~40% of total vehicle cost.

2. **Recycling scale**: GAST predicts the recyclable battery market will approach 150GWh by 2025 in China, with a forecast model shown for retiring battery volumes and growth rates.

3. **Recycling models**: Among 240+ companies claiming battery recycling operations, only 27 are on the national whitelist. A platform-based approach with clear division of labor and fair profit distribution is recommended.

4. **Value realization**: Full lifecycle value optimization requires extending battery life through control strategy improvements, reducing cascade utilization costs (via BMS management, low-cost cell grouping, local application to cut transport costs), and lowering scrap processing costs through scale and automation.

5. **Cascade utilization factors**: Key considerations include battery performance requirements, cost analysis, and market scale. Core performance indicators involve safety/performance, cell grouping technology, and data systems.

6. **Applicable scenarios**: Lithium batteries (3x energy density, 2x lifespan of lead-acid) are best suited to replace lead-acid batteries in backup power and low-performance power battery applications.

7. **Design for recyclability**: Modular designs for easier disassembly, standardized sizes, enhanced BMS monitoring, information traceability, and "battery-vehicle separation" designs can improve recycling value.

8. **Multi-stage vs. single-stage utilization**: Single-stage utilization is economically superior—LFP batteries yield max 272 yuan/kWh in single use versus 54.9 yuan/kWh in two-stage cascade use. N-level cascade utilization is currently not viable.

9. **Scrap value**: Lithium recovery from LFP batteries yields minimum 0.7万元/ton; cobalt recovery from NCM811 batteries yields minimum 1.14万元/ton at 95%+ recovery efficiency. China is projected to achieve 70% cobalt self-supply through recycling by 2025.

10. **LFP vs. ternary batteries**: LFP batteries excel in cascade utilization (due to long lifespan), while ternary batteries are better suited for direct material recovery (due to higher rare metal content), though ternary batteries can also be reused in low-performance applications.

**Business Model Recommendations:**
- Vehicle manufacturers (OEMs) play a decisive role in the recycling value chain through dealer networks, battery monitoring capabilities, and application scenario design
- A "1+1+1" ecosystem model (OEM/alliance + professional company + end-use customers) is proposed
- OEMs should focus on overall ecosystem planning and value chain integration rather than direct recycling operations ("专业的人做专业的事" - professionals doing professional work)

**Additional Context**: The website also features other recent GAST insights including 2026 Chinese auto market analysis, 2026 H2 industry trend predictions, and a global automotive supply chain competitiveness report (2026) co-released with China Automotive News.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"动力电池回收利用是一个涉及法规、环境、技术、商业价值及商业模式等多方面的综合领域，在不同的阶段具备不同的价值体现。" - The article's framing of battery recycling as a comprehensive field.
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 15: 梯次利用储能项目被叫停背后：动力电池迎“退役潮”，2025年将达78万吨 ---
URL: http://www.nbd.com.cn/rss/toutiao/articles/1817852.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from 每日经济新闻 (National Business Daily) reports on China's power battery "retirement wave" (动力电池退役潮) as the country's first batch of new energy vehicle power batteries reaches end-of-life. Key data points include: China accumulated approximately 200,000 tons of retired power batteries in 2020, projected to reach 780,000 tons by 2025; China had about 5.8 million new energy vehicles as of May (roughly 50% of the global total); power battery installations totaled 63.6 GWh in 2020 (up 2.3% year-on-year); and cumulative retirements from 2020-2022 are expected to reach 90.5 GWh. Oriental Securities forecasts the battery echelon utilization and recycling market could reach 37 billion yuan by 2025.

The article discusses two main recycling methods: element recovery (extracting heavy metals like manganese, lithium, cobalt, and nickel from ternary lithium and lithium iron phosphate batteries) and cascade/echelon utilization (reusing retired battery packs in smaller applications like low-speed EVs, power tools, solar street lights, or combining packs for solar/wind energy storage).

Key issues and expert perspectives highlighted include:
1. Safety concerns: Professor 康龙 (South China University of Technology) notes cascade utilization extends battery lifespan and helps with grid frequency/peak regulation but cannot fundamentally solve pollution issues and poses fire safety risks.
2. Standardization problems: Batteries are customized per automaker with varying structures, specifications, and parameters, making automated disassembly difficult—some complex battery packs risk short circuits, leaks, or even explosions if mishandled.
3. Testing challenges: Professor 康龙 emphasizes the need for accurate battery identification (SOH, SOC, SOP) to screen out defective cells before reuse.
4. Cost and regulation gaps: 吴奔奔 (Guangdong Bangpu Cycle Technology) notes a lack of coordinated supervision and imperfect reward/punishment mechanisms in the recycling industry.
5. Illegal recycling channels: 于清教 (Zhongguancun New Battery Technology Innovation Alliance) reveals that small unregulated workshops dominate over 50% of the market by offering higher prices, and even licensed recyclers purchase batteries from these workshops.
6. Timeline: Batteries from the early "Ten Cities, Thousand Vehicles" program (installed 2018-2022) and those mass-installed during 2014-2016 subsidy policies are now reaching retirement, with the latter expected to be replaced within two years.

The article notes China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has issued several policies on retired battery comprehensive utilization and released a draft "Measures for Cascade Utilization Management of New Energy Vehicle Power Batteries" in October 2020, making echelon utilization a policy priority. However, industry consensus on whether to pursue direct recycling or cascade utilization remains divided, with debate centered on safety, economics, and reliability—particularly for ternary lithium batteries which degrade more significantly after repeated charge cycles. Researcher 肖成伟 (China Electronics Technology Group Corporation 18th Research Institute) advocates using big data to track battery health and safety, noting estimation methods and control strategies for retired batteries differ from those used in vehicles.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"动力电池梯次利用十分有益，但也存在隐患：好处是可以延长电池使用（寿命）周期，缓解环境污染的压力。同时，梯次利用的电池也可参与电力系统调频、调峰，提高电能质量。但梯次利用不能根本性解决环境污染问题，电池的废弃与回收仍会到来。此外，还有一个问题是存在消防安全隐患。"——华南理工大学教授康龙
</key_excerpts>

# 纯电、增程和插混，哪种动力形式才是未来？

###### 2025年11月21日 08:28   21世纪经济报道 21财经APP   焦文娟

**21世纪经济报道记者 焦文娟 广州报道**

管永超从用户角度回答了这一趋势。他认为，当前消费者对大容量电池带来的使用体验普遍持认可态度。然而他也强调，国内用车场景具有高度复杂性，需因地制宜看待不同动力方案。

和前三家车企不同的是，蔚来是当前国内唯一一家只做纯电的车企。而对于未来的解法，蔚来的答案是坚定不移做纯电。蔚来俞斌称，不管是做增程、纯电还是混动，核心还是在解决用户的续航焦虑。

“大电池持续增加我认为不可取，可能会在一个度上停下来。大家共同努力的应该是如何解除用户最后那1%的焦虑。从未来的思考来讲，换电可能对大部分场景是一个终极解法。”

#### 以下是本次圆桌会谈实录，内容经摘编：

**21世纪经济报道：当下，汽车创新百花齐放。既有纯电、超级插混，也有超级增程，今天我们邀请到四位车企技术领域的领军人，来聊聊哪种动力形式才是未来？首先我们来聊一聊大电池。如今无论是纯电、超级增程还是超级插混，电池容量都越来越大，电池是不是越大越好？更大的电池是否牺牲了一些其他功能或者体验？**

**曹力：**我个人觉得未来的方向肯定是纯电，要不然为什么新能源往电池这个方向去做，因为它带来更多的其实是体验更好，然后使用成本低，包括对于环境排放污染这块（也更好），就是将来这肯定是大方向，对吧？所以从我自己的角度来说，我觉得大的方向上肯定是纯电。

但纯电在基础设施、体验，包括续航焦虑这些问题，其实一直都存在。所以到底选什么技术路线，用多大的电池，我觉得还是要回到用户的实际需求。比如说像我，平时主要在长三角活动，自己开车也就几百公里范围，现在的续航对我来说已经够用了。

而且现在高压快充和高速上的充电设施也挺全的，对很多用户来说，可能就会直接选纯电产品。但确实也有很多用户，可能是出于习惯，或者经常跑长途，或者对纯电的体验还在观望，抱着试试看的心态。那这个时候，混动就是一个很好的补充选择。

事实也证明，从渗透率和用户购买量来看，混动产品其实占比还是非常高的。所以未来几年，在能源形式这方面，我觉得纯电和混动应该还是会保持互补、并存的状态。

说到底，我们还是要回到用户具体的使用场景是怎样的，再来决定我们到底该配多大的电池。当然，大电池也会带来一些技术瓶颈，比如重量会更大，又有电池、又有发动机、又有直驱系统，控制起来肯定会更复杂。所以这也要求我们在技术，包括控制策略上要做更多优化，通过创新去提升这类产品的体验。

**祁宏钟：**首先刚才曹总说得很好，电池用不用大的，关键还是看用户需求。但另一方面，大电池也确实带来一系列挑战。比如电池做大，体积就会变大，重量也会增加，这就需要更大的安装空间，这就意味着，那些小轴距的小型车，它可能就满足不了。

如果电量很大，你必须要把车造得更大，车造得更重。车子更重，那么带来更大的挑战就是对道路的损伤也会很大——虽然目前还不明显。因此，电池的大小一方面确实是取决于用户的诉求，另外也取决于我们这边的条件。

所以说我们初步分析下来，对于不同级别的车，或者不同使用区域的车，确实有不同的更适合的路线。

但我们国家的能源结构正快速向以电为主演化，这就决定了我们国家一定是以电为主的驱动形式，肯定会是主流。我们认为电动肯定是个主流，只是在电动不适用的场景和车型上，需要更好的解决方案。因此插电和增程就作为一种补充形式出现。

这种情况下，比如北方地区、高原地区、偏远地区，包括国际市场，充电设施不到位的时候，就会出现各种各样的诉求和需求变化。

因此针对您的问题“是不是电池越大越好”，答案肯定是看需求。在国内满足需求的情况下，用户觉得开得更舒服的话，电量肯定是越大越好。

但在一些充电不方便、车型可能也做不大，或者其他场景，电池可能要适当。电池适当的话，续航就不够了，这时候就要考虑插电和增程的补充方案。

所以说结论就是：根据需求来定，电池在需求范围内越大越好。

**管永超：**最终的决定权还是在用户这块，最终买单的是用户。

站在用户的角度，插混车型或者增程车型基本上解决了纯电车型长途旅行能耗和续航的焦虑，但是在一定程度上，我们原来是100公里或者150公里甚至80公里这种级别的续航用户需要经常充电，就带来了充电的焦虑，把电池电量加上去之后，虽然说成本略有增加，当然现在电池的成本跟以前相比已经大大下降了，所以成本的增加用户感知已经不敏感了，但能给用户带来什么？他原来一周充两次电变成一周充一次电了，原来一周充一次电可能两周充一次电，今年各家企业推出的插电增程的300公里、350公里甚至到500公里，到这个级别之后，如果经常上下班的用户他真的开这个车跟纯电的没有什么差异，仅仅是在放假的时候，需要长途旅行的时候才会用到增程或者插混的场景，在其他场景下都是以纯电的方式在运行，用户的驾驶体验也是非常好。

用户对于更大的电量、更大的电池在使用体验方面还是比较认可的，但我们看到，在国内的场景是非常复杂的，不光是南方，还有广大的北方，还有西部区域，他的充电设施没那么方便，冬天的时候低温又限制了电池性能的发挥，还有越野车，越野车追求的场景都在户外，这种场景下充电也没那么方便。所以针对不同的场景下需要不同的解决方案，针对不同的用户也可能有不同的解决方案。

**21世纪经济报道：以往插混相比增程的优势是发动机直驱车辆。但现在很多超级增程出现了，发动机的热效率和动力也更强了。所以超级插混和超级增程是否有融合的趋势？如果消费者要购买，如何在这两种动力形式中做出选择？**

**祁宏钟：**这个问题确实很纠结，在我们整个研发过程中也一直很纠结这个课题。

广汽最早2017年就量产过插电车，2014年量产过增程车，真是老兵。我基本上见证了新能源混动系统整个发展历程，每个阶段都有不同挑战。走到今天，制约的短板基本都补齐了。从最早没有好电池、好发动机、好增程器、好电控，到今天我们的电池、电机、电控都做得非常好，发动机水平也很高。

这种情况下就会出现，你在做一台车时选哪套动力系统，这套系统的差异到底有多大，该选哪个。这还是回到刚才的问题：如果只是普通使用，包括城市通勤、城际运行，甚至像我春节从广州回老家一千多公里，实际上差异并不是很大。当然我指的是正常驾驶、正常路径、正常高速。

差异出现在比较极端的情况，比如持续爬坡、高温环境、高原，这种情况下差异很明显。但现在的实际情况是，绝大部分用户遇不到这些情况。如果非要说这两条路线对用户有多大差异，可能体现在一些跑越野的用户，或者像我们测试到海拔很高、很冷的地方，才会出现差异。

所以我们觉得，对不同级别、不同用户群，优先顺序应该是：如果可以，一般会先选电车；再有焦虑或某些极端工况不满足时，会往后退。作为补充的就是插电和增程。要说最全面的话，目前是插电最全面的一套系统。但对用户来说，如果抛开极端工况，都是足够用的。这是目前为止我们的理解。

**管永超：**其实刚才祁总说的，在东风这边我们也深有感触。技术发展到现在，无论是发动机、电驱、电池，尤其是能量管理和控制各方面，已经非常先进。所以对常规用户来说，无论是开插混还是增程，实际上很难感知出区别。

但在技术层面，两者确实存在差异。增程也就是串联，其实只是插混中的一种工作模式。多出来的工作模式，在技术上是有其优势的，只是用户不一定都能体验到。

但如果你真的跑到特定场景下，这种优势就能体现出来。比如在越野场景，尤其是这两年增长非常快的“方盒子”车型领域，有很多脱困工况和复杂路况。这时候如果有一个直驱档，尤其低速直驱档，它带来的优势是增程难以比拟的。

所以，插混和增程怎么选，怎么满足用户需求，还是要看不同级别、不同车型定位。对大多数普通消费者来说，很难感知出差异，但在差异化场景中，优势还是能体现出来的。 

如果你买车主要在城市里用，很少跑高速，日常范围就两三百公里，那纯电就够；如果有点焦虑，增程或插混都可以。如果经常跑高速、常去户外，那插混相比增程能在能耗上带来额外收益。

**21世纪经济报道：去年有个声音是说零跑能成黑马的原因是增程救了零跑，但去年我研究了一下，零跑的纯电是比增程卖得更好的，今年零跑在超级增程上有发力，用户选择零跑是选择纯电版本更好，还是买一辆超级增程车更好？**

**曹力：**从数据上来说，用户在选择零跑的时候，现在的数据是纯电已经接近80%了。

增程会作为一个在大车里面相对来说用户会青睐一点的选项，因为大车比如C16、D19，大车的使用场景有更强烈的长途需求，虽然实际上大家一年也跑不了几次长途，但这个诉求比小车要强烈一点，所以大车的比例会更高一点，比如C16会超过30%，D19从目前用户的选择来看，可能会超过40%，还是看用户的诉求。从整体的零跑的动力形式上看，用户还是会更加倾向零跑电车的属性会更强。

**21世纪经济报道：刚过去的10月，纯电动市场零售同比增长，增程、插混同比下降，汽车市场呈现“纯电高歌，插混增程疲软”的状态。所以，未来属于纯电吗？还是这只是超级增程和超级插混黎明前的黑暗？**

**俞斌：** 我们一直很坚定在做纯电，未来我们也不会做增程或者插混。可能在前几年的时候，包括电池有一段时间价格高企，包括增程在一定时间内，在基建还没有完善的时候，确实解决了用户的焦虑，但产品规划在所有产品里面都会有滞后性，一般性车厂可能快一点20几个月，慢一点三四十个月的时间，可能他在2021年的时候做了立项，

那时候看到纯电和增程之间有些摇摆，那时候立项以后，咱们今天看到新的产品出现了，他的决策路径是几年前的路径。不管是动力体系的比较，1%的场景里面我们进一步解决这里面的尖点问题，因为中国主流车都是家庭用车，99%的用户就是城市高速，如果我们坚定地选择了纯电路线往前走，实际上我们还是觉得用户会选择更好的场景，现在纯电一套体系，油一套体系， 本质上来说还是很贵的，而且加电池的成本，都在加，你失去的东西不少，刚才再次强调车重会变重，其实车重变重不是简单的重，是整个车的体系、动力体系、散热体系全在成本里增加，最后这些钱还是回到市场上，反映到用户的支付成本上去。

第二点，在用户体验上，如果两套体系在车上面，必须有地方安装这些东西，所以重量增加。虽然我们知道各位在全力以赴把电池变小，但毕竟有将近200L空间，把这个空间放车上，用户可能一年用一两次，但大部分的时候他痛点是用户真正要全家出行的时候就是跑长途、过年或者寒暑假，人多、东西放不下了，要不车做得特别大，但中国的道路情况不可能一直持续这样下去，有时候停车并不是那么容易。我们想要解决的问题是真正还原到用户的场景里面，车能不能做得性价比高一些，我们说的性价比是支付的能力，买到他真正想要的东西，而不是为了小场景去支付成本，包括他想要的人坐得舒服，空间坐得舒服，这些点上我们能不能做得更好一些。我们把增程器拿掉以后就会有前备舱，大家已经意识到这个事情是未来的方向。

从产品的角度来讲，第一，你永远是要为用户真正解决问题，不管是体验还是成本，都是用户想要的东西。第二，技术路径上，大家看得更终局一些，包括从体系的方法去解题，而不是单独从产品定义的方式解题，这也是未来几年里面我觉得中国的新能源行业要共识的核心点。

**管永超：**终局的目标应该是往电的方向发展，在国内这块肯定是没什么问题的，只是现在纯电还有一些问题，当然整个行业都在解决，出现增程还有插电，有它们的市场，在目前这个环节，尤其未来5-10年，还是能够解决一些用户遇到的问题。随着未来电池技术的发展，以及基础设施包括小区的改造等等，纯电的比例会越来越高，这个是大趋势，这是任何一个企业都能看到的。

第二个在目前的情况下，电池成本也下降了很多，很多企业虽然是增程的或者插混的车大家也在不断地提高电量，让这个车像电车的驾驶感受，使用发动机或者使用插混的几率确实不断地降低，尤其这两年大家都在喊“大电小油”，很多车企在践行这个方向，尤其更多的企业在开发更小的增程器，更小的发动机，很多用户还是会有需求，他的需求如果满足不了，那他买了这个车不敢做一些事情，比如过年的时候没法开纯电车回家，或者开纯电车回家路上会碰到小的不愉快，在一定的时间范围内，插电和增程还会继续存在，并且大家为这个方向去开发更小的发动机、增程器来减少成本上的增量，来减少车辆重量增加的问题。在满足客户的需求方面，我们不管是做增程的、插混还是纯电的，大家的方向是一致的。在这个过程中，我们跟行业一道，站在消费者的角度，尽量去满足各种各样的需求，让用户在买车的时候能够放心地去选。

尤其是去年出海，我们已经接近600万辆，今年会更高，除了国内的用户，未来各个企业可能要考虑国外怎么办，我们不可能一直在国内，我们肯定是要走出国门，我们把插混和增程的技术做好，到海外这块，他的性能空间会更加广阔。

**21世纪经济报道：既然大家都觉得，纯电是未来，那增程和插混的机会到底有多久呢？**

**祁宏钟：**终局是电动，这个共识没有任何问题。现在在电的安全和补能方式没有彻底解决之前，用户还是有其他诉求的，如何来满足这些需求？这就是增程和插电存在的意义。等到彻底解决的时候，可能就出现了归一的情况。

现在的问题是如何能在这个阶段内做到又满足用户需求，又把这个车做得又小又轻，最终一定是在满足用户的需求下，把车做得更轻更节能，这是既能满足用户又能满足国家和社会发展最好的结局。但现在来看，在这一点上还是有很多的挑战，包括做研发做技术的基本都在应对这些问题。

增程和插电有什么机会？我觉得还是有的，目前没有解决掉的北方市场，包括国际化也是我们重点考虑对象，离开中国之后你会发现补能条件，包括电费、售后维护等等挑战非常大，中国在这方面目前是遥遥领先的。应对国外那么多复杂的市场的时候，很多地方还是油车为主，用什么去占领它？我在思考，当我们把充电作为主攻方向去攻克，把技术降级使用到增程和插电上来是一个路径。

另外，对于国际化的市场，我们用插电和增程技术降维打击，去争夺市场也是很好的趋势，既能满足国内市场，又能把国外充电的问题解决掉，这个可能才是我们最终的出路。最终可能是中国遥遥领先，纯电为主的社会，国外也许是以增程、插电小电池的社会，会形成这样的全球动力能源格局，在二三十年之内应该不会有大的问题。

**21世纪经济报道：曹总，很多人都像零跑一样进行双重技术路线的版本，您对这些后进入者有什么想说的吗？**

曹力：我觉得不存在早晚的话题。很多人问现在做增程会不会太晚，其实都是为了解决用户续航焦虑这个问题。

不管是纯电、增程、插电混动还是换电，都是在解决同一道题目。关于技术是否先进，我一直认为合适的就是最先进的。

这几种方式各有优劣势：增程在极限工况或高速情况下，可能因没有直驱而在亏电油耗或NVH方面有所牺牲；混动系统又比增程更复杂，零部件更多；换电模式则需要前期大投入，结构成本也需考虑能否在车型上覆盖。

最终都是为了满足用户需求。不能只看国内市场——虽然国内条件很好，但海外每个地区条件不同：有些地方路况差，轿车都难正常使用；充电设施、油电价格比、政策环境都不一样。

我们的技术应该在适应用户需求的同时，放眼全球，适应不同市场竞争。这个方向上还有很大空间。

- 曹力 (Cao Li) from Leapmotor (零跑): Believes pure electric is the overall direction, but plug-in hybrids (PHEV) and extended-range (EREV) will coexist with EVs for the next several years. - 祁宏钟 (Qi Hongzhong) from GAC (广汽): An industry veteran who has witnessed the entire PHEV/EREV development history since GAC's first PHEV in 2017 and EREV in 2014. Views electric drive as the mainstream given China's electricity-centric energy structure, with PHEV/EREV as supplements for scenarios where charging infrastructure is lacking (northern regions, plateaus, remote areas, international markets).
- 管永超 (Guan Yongchao) from Dongfeng (东风): Emphasizes that PHEV/EREV technology has greatly reduced charging frequency for users (from twice a week to once a week or less). Notes that "large battery, small engine" is the current trend. Highlights the importance of international markets, with Chinese auto exports approaching 6 million units last year.
- 俞斌 (Yu Bin) from NIO (蔚来): The only participant whose company is purely electric. Firmly committed to pure electric and will not do EREV or PHEV. Argues that dual powertrain systems add cost and weight (nearly 200L of space), while battery swap technology may be the ultimate solution for range anxiety.

Key discussion themes:
1. Whether bigger batteries are always better - conclusion: depends on user needs and scenarios; batteries should be as large as needed within requirements.
2. Whether super PHEV and super EREV are converging - the technical differences are hard to perceive for most users, but PHEV's direct-drive advantage is significant in off-road and extreme conditions.
3. Market data from October 2025 shows pure EV retail sales growing year-over-year while EREV and PHEV declined, prompting debate on whether this indicates the future belongs to pure electric.
4. Consensus that the ultimate endgame is electrification, but PHEV/EREV will persist for 5-10 years or more, especially for northern China markets and international expansion where charging infrastructure is inadequate.

Key influential data points from the discussion include that only about 1% of user scenarios involve extreme conditions where technical differences between powertrain types manifest clearly.
args.key_excerpts: 曹力: "我个人觉得未来的方向肯定是纯电...但纯电在基础设施、体验，包括续航焦虑这些问题，其实一直都存在。所以到底选什么技术路线，用多大的电池，我觉得还是要回到用户的实际需求。"

新能源汽车是指采用非常规车用燃料作为动力来源，技术原理先进、具有新技术、新结构的汽车，它包括纯电动汽车、插电式混合动力汽车、增程式电动汽车、燃料电池汽车等，而其中增程式电动汽车是我们今天要讲的主角。

电动汽车资源网了解到，今年实施的新版电动汽车术语，对增程式电动汽车做了以下定义：一种在纯电动模式下可以达到其所有的动力性能，而当车载可充电储能系统无法满足续航里程要求时，打开车载辅助供电装置为动力系统提供电能，以延长续航里程的电动汽车，且该车载辅助供电装置与驱动系统没有传动轴（带）等传动连接。

什么是增程式呢？从字面上来看，就是“增加续航里程”，也就是解决纯电动车里程焦虑。从工作原理来说，增程式电动汽车只靠电机来驱动车轮，增程器并不会直接驱动车轮，仅仅用来发电。在电动汽车电池电量不足时，通过增程器向车辆输入一定的外部能量，使车辆能够继续行驶。增程器可以是燃油发动机，还可以是天然气、醇燃料、氢燃料发动机。增程器发出的电力能传送给汽车的电池储存起来，也能提供给电动机用于驱动车轮。用雪佛兰volt做例子，其纯电续航里程为85km，用专用240V电线充电需要4．5小时左右；当电池电量消耗完，1．5升的汽油发动机增程器就会成为发电机，为电力引擎供电。

增程式电动汽车的工作原理有以下几种：一，外接充电模式，即在停车的时候为电池充电；二，纯电动模式，当电动汽车电池电量充足时，电池为电动机提供电能来驱动车轮行驶；三，增程式工作模式，当电池电量不足时，由发动机发电，向电池充电或者直接供给电动机驱动车轮。

电动汽车资源网之所以认为应该重视增程式电动汽车，是因为它有以下几大优点：

一，油耗低，因为发动机只负责充电，所以只要一个排量很小的发动机即可完成工作。

二，续航有保障，电池电量消耗完毕之后，增程器变成发电机，为电动机提供电力，这也就有效解决了当下大家普遍关心的里程焦虑问题。

三，噪音极小，由于增程器排量极小，在其工作时，发出的噪音非常低。

四，增程式电动汽车和纯电动汽车一样技术难度相对较低，因为两者都是单纯的“电驱动”，增程式电动汽车上的发动机不需要介入驱动系统，也就不用考虑复杂的模式切换。

增程式电动汽车目前在国内还没有引起特别大的关注，但目前已有不少企业投身其中，其技术路线也越来越多样化，有的企业专注于研发汽油和柴油发动机增程器，有的企业专注于研发乙醇发动机增程器，有的企业专注于研发燃料电池发动机增程器，还有的企业研发出了燃气轮机增程器。目前国内的增程式电动汽车研究内容主要是乘用车增程器专用发动机设计与控制、高效发电机系统、增程器系统集成等技术；开发体积小、比油耗低、综合效率高的增程器专用发动机和增程器系统；开展整车集成技术与一体化最优控制技术研究。

纵观全局，增程式电动汽车在国内还处于刚刚起步的阶段，许多企业还停留在样车开发时期，要将增程式电动汽车工程化、产业化还有一段路要走。电动汽车资源网认为，中国作为目前全球最大的汽车市场，汽车产业正处于一个十分关键的转型时期，对于包括增程式电动汽车在内的任何一种有可能成功的汽车技术路线，都需要关注且研究，这样才能找出最适合我国汽车产业发展的技术路线。

This is a Chinese-language blog post published on the Infineon Developer Community on July 29, 2018, by user "糖糖爱学习" (Level 0). The article is an educational piece (科普文) explaining the concept and advantages of Extended-Range Electric Vehicles (EREVs / 增程式电动汽车).

Key content:
- EREVs are defined (under the new 2018 EV terminology standard) as electric vehicles that can achieve all their driving performance in pure electric mode, and when the onboard rechargeable energy storage system cannot meet range requirements, an onboard auxiliary power unit provides electricity to the powertrain to extend driving range. Importantly, the auxiliary power unit has NO mechanical transmission connection (shaft/belt) to the drive system.
- Working principle: EREVs are driven only by electric motors; the range extender (增程器) does not directly drive the wheels—it only generates electricity. When battery power runs low, the range extender supplies external energy to keep the vehicle moving. Range extenders can use gasoline, natural gas, alcohol fuel, or hydrogen fuel engines. Generated electricity can be stored in the battery or fed directly to the motor.
- Example cited: Chevrolet Volt has an 85 km pure electric range, takes ~4.5 hours to charge via a dedicated 240V line; after battery depletion, its 1.5L gasoline engine acts as a generator.
- Three operating modes: (1) External charging mode (charging battery while parked), (2) Pure electric mode (battery powers motor when fully charged), (3) Range-extended mode (engine generates electricity to charge battery or directly power the motor when battery is low).

Four advantages highlighted:
1. Low fuel consumption—only a small-displacement engine is needed since it only charges the battery.
2. Guaranteed range—the range extender becomes a generator after battery depletion, solving range anxiety.
3. Very low noise—the small-displacement range extender produces minimal noise.
4. Lower technical difficulty compared to other hybrid types—both EREVs and pure EVs are purely "electric-driven," so the engine doesn't need to engage the drive system, avoiding complex mode-switching.

Industry status: EREVs have received limited attention in China but multiple companies are investing. Technology routes are diversifying—some companies focus on gasoline/diesel engine extenders, others on ethanol engines, fuel cell engines, or gas turbine extenders. Current domestic research focuses on dedicated range extender engine design and control for passenger vehicles, high-efficiency generator systems, range extender system integration, and vehicle-level integration with optimized integrated control. The technology is still in its early stages in China, with many companies at the prototype development stage; engineering and industrialization still have a long way to go.

The article originates from 电动汽车资源网 (Electric Vehicle Resources Network). The post has 2,744 views and 2 comments. The blog is tagged under "行业资讯" (Industry News).

# 性能车超快充技术怎么选？2026年800V新车21.99万起，10分钟补能500公里成现实

性能车超快充技术怎么选？2026年800V新车21.99万起，10分钟补能500公里成现实

2026年08月06日 12:55 看点资讯

[语音播报](javascript:; "语音播报") [缩小字体](javascript:; "缩小字体") [放大字体](javascript:; "放大字体") [微博](javascript:; "分享到微博") [微信](javascript:; "分享到微信") [分享](javascript:; "更多分享") [0](javascript:;)

2026年，性能车超快充技术迎来爆发，800V高压平台新车最低21.99万元起，仰望U7 EV版实现充电10分钟补能503公里，性能、续航与快充的“不可能三角”被打破。本文结合智车星球、汽车之家等公开报道，盘点2026年超快充性能车的价格区间与购车成本。

2026年，随着5C/6C倍率电池大规模量产和800V/900V高压平台普及，“充电10分钟，续航数百公里”逐渐成为新能源车新常态。智车星球在网易发布《充电比加油快？2026超快充新车大盘点！》[1]，对小米SU7、蔚来ES9、极氪8X、理想L9等车型的超快充配置和预计价格进行了梳理；汽车之家车家号则报道了仰望U7 2026款，其搭载第二代刀片电池与闪充技术，打破了高性能电动车“性能、续航、快充”的不可能三角[2]。本文基于这两份公开资料，结合购车成本视角，为你拆解超快充性能车的价格真相。

性能车超快充技术普及到什么程度？20万级也能享受800V吗？

能。2026年，800V高压平台已经不再是豪华品牌专属，20万级车型开始标配。据智车星球盘点，智己L6全系标配800V高压平台（部分早期入门款除外），预售价格21.99-30.59万元，顶配“光年版”更是搭载133kWh半固态电池，CLTC续航1002公里，支持12分钟补能400公里[1]。小米SU7 2026款标准版和Pro版采用752V碳化硅高压平台，Max版采用897V碳化硅高压平台，预计售价22.99-30.99万元[1]。这意味着，过去高性能纯电车动辄40万以上的入门门槛，如今被拉低到22万元以内。

从行业趋势看，800V平台从“加分项”变成“标配”，甚至出现了900V。资料显示，蔚来ES9、极氪8X等车型已经冲向900V[1]。这种技术下放，不仅提升了充电速度，也改善了整车能耗效率。对于消费者而言，20多万预算已经能买到此前30-40万才有的充电体验。不过，部分车型的入门版本可能未配备超快充，比如智己L6部分早期入门款。因此购车时需仔细查看配置表，确认是否为800V。

过去，800V平台多见于保时捷Taycan等百万级车型。如今，国内供应链成熟，碳化硅功率器件成本下降，5C/6C电池量产，使得超快充技术能够快速下放。这也是智己L6、小米SU7等车型能压到20万级的原因。对于预算有限的性能车爱好者，2026年是入手超快充车型的好时机。

不同价位的超快充性能车，充电速度和续航差多少？

价位越高，充电倍率和系统电压越高，补能速度越快；但20万级与百万级的差距并没有想象中悬殊。从公开报道来看：20万级车型中，智己L6光年版12分钟补能400公里，小米SU7 Max 15分钟补能670公里；30-50万级中，吉利银河星舰10分钟补能80%，魏牌V9X充电5分钟补能200公里；50万级中，理想L9 Livis版10分钟补能500公里，岚图泰山Ultra 20%-80%电量快充仅需12分钟[1]。百万级中，尊界M900充电5分钟补能200公里，而仰望U7 EV版充电10分钟可增加503公里续航[2]。

从数据看，20万级车型的10分钟补能大约在400公里左右，百万级也在500公里上下，差距在30%以内。但高价车型往往配备更大电池、更高电压平台和更强热管理，在极寒环境下的表现更稳定。例如仰望U7 PHEV在零下30°C充电时间仅比常温多3分钟[2]。

需要注意的是，官方标注的补能里程多为特定环境下的理论值。实际使用中，充电功率会随电池电量上升而下降，尤其是在电量超过80%后，充电速度明显放缓。因此，日常快充建议将电量控制在20%-80%区间，这既节省时间，也有利于电池健康。

买超快充性能车，除了车价还要花哪些钱？电池买断VS租用怎么选？

除了裸车价，还需考虑保险、选装、上牌、充电设施以及电池方案；电池租用能降低首付，但长期成本未必低于买断。以表格中的车型为例，包牌落地价一般等于指导价+保险+上牌费。目前国内新能源车免征购置税政策仍在延续，但2026年具体政策需以财政部、税务总局最新公告为准。如果选装更大电池、高阶智驾或空气悬架，费用会进一步增加。比如智己L6光年版比入门版高出约8.6万元，但换来半固态电池和1002公里续航[1]。

对于电池方案，部分品牌提供电池租赁。以蔚来为代表的换电模式，通常可以将购车价降低数万元，但每月需支付租金。对于计划开3-5年且看重换电便利性的用户，租用更划算；对于长期持有用户，买断电池的二手车残值更高，总成本可能更低。需以各品牌官方实时方案为准。

除了基础购车成本，各地政府的新能源汽车消费补贴也可能影响最终落地价。例如，部分省份对报废旧车并购买新能源车的用户给予一次性补贴，金额从数千元到两万元不等。具体以当地商务部门发布的最新通知为准。此外，部分品牌提供置换补贴或低息金融方案，购车时需主动询问，并对比不同渠道的报价。

另外，超快充车型需要大功率充电桩。如果家里有固定车位，建议安装11kW或更高功率的私桩，安装费用约数千元；如果依赖公共快充，则需要关注充电桩峰值功率是否匹配车型。据公开信息，目前主流的480kW液冷超充桩正在加速普及，但部分地区覆盖仍有限。

超快充对电池寿命有影响吗？二手车残值会受影响吗？

超快充不会必然缩短电池寿命，但电池健康度将成为二手车定价的核心指标。很多人担心“充电5分钟”会伤电池。实际上，车企通过电芯材料、热管理和BMS算法来保障循环寿命。例如，仰望U7搭载的第二代刀片电池配合闪充技术，官方宣称在极寒环境下依然能快速充电[2]；极氪自研金砖电池能量密度较麒麟电池提升约15%，配合6C超充[1]。这些技术的目的就是在高倍率充电时控制发热和析锂，延长电池寿命。

不过，从物理规律看，高倍率充放电确实会加速电池老化。因此，在二手车市场，超快充车型的检测评估会更依赖电池健康度数据。目前行业尚无统一的电池衰减国家标准，建议购车时关注厂家对电池质保的承诺。例如，多数品牌提供8年或16万公里以上的电池质保。具体条款需以官方质保手册为准。

舆论场中，有网友质疑“超快充是牺牲寿命换速度”，也有观点认为“技术成熟后无需担心”。目前尚无大规模超快充车型的长距离使用数据，建议保持观望并选择大品牌产品。

目前，行业内对超快充的定义尚未统一，通常指充电倍率3C以上或10分钟补能200公里以上。2026年的新车普遍将5C作为卖点，但5C倍率需要600kW以上充电桩支持。因此，购车前可通过充电App查询周边是否有适配的超级充电桩，避免“有车无桩”。

2026年有哪些超快充性能车值得关注？购车成本怎么算？

从21.99万到150万，超快充性能车已覆盖多价位段，购车时应综合参考裸车价、电池方案、充电条件和优惠政策。以下根据公开报道整理了8款代表性车型的参考价格与核心配置：

| 车型/版本 | 参考价 | 核心配置 | 适合人群 | 注意点 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 智己L6光年版 | 21.99-30.59万 | 800V、133kWh半固态、CLTC 1002km、12分钟补能400km | 追求长续航和快充的轿跑用户 | 部分入门款非800V；实际价格以官方为准 |
| 小米SU7 Max | 预计22.99-30.99万 | 897V碳化硅、15分钟补能670km、激光雷达 | 智能+性能爱好者 | 预计2026年4月上市，需确认交付节奏 |
| 吉利银河星舰 | 30-45万 | 6C超充、77kWh、10分钟补能80%、插混 | 家庭多人出行 | 插混车型亏电油耗待实测 |
| 极氪8X | 35-50万 | 900V、6C超充、1030kW、金砖电池 | 高性能SUV玩家 | 三电机版或为插混，价格可能更高 |
| 岚图泰山Ultra | 45.99万起 | 800V 5C、20%-80%约12分钟、L3智驾 | 对智驾和空间有要求的家庭 | L3功能依赖法规和OTA |
| 奔驰纯电GLC | 45-65万 | 800V、10分钟补能300km、WLTP约800km | 豪华品牌燃油车用户 | 实际续航与官方WLTP有差距 |
| 理想L9 Livis版 | 55.98万 | 800V 5C、10分钟补能500km、增程 | 增程+大空间需求 | 增程结构需加油，纯电续航400km |
| 尊界M900 | 90-150万 | 800V碳化硅、三电机750kW、5分钟补能200km | 超豪华SUV买家 | 品牌知名度仍需沉淀 |

以上价格均为公开报道的参考价或预计售价，实际落地价需以官方及经销商实时信息为准。购车决策时，建议用“裸车价+保险+上牌费+选装+电池方案”计算综合持有成本，并关注各地新能源置换补贴和充电权益。例如，部分城市对置换新能源车提供1-2万元补贴，具体需查询当地政策。

接下来值得关注的是蔚来ES9、极氪8X、广汽埃安Hyper昊铂旗舰系列等车型的最终定价和交付。随着900V平台和半固态电池的量产，超快充性能车的技术天花板还将继续抬升。同时，充电基础设施的升级速度将决定超快充体验能否真正普及。建议消费者在购车时优先选择已经建成品牌超充网络的车企，如蔚来、小鹏、极氪等。

QA：性能车超快充技术常见问题

Q1：性能车超快充技术现在最低多少钱能买到？

A1：目前800V超快充新车最低21.99万元起，代表车型是智己L6；小米SU7 2026款预计22.99万元起。部分品牌提供电池租赁方案，购车门槛会更低，具体以官方实时信息为准。

Q2：充电10分钟，实际能跑多少公里？

A2：2026年主流超快充车型的10分钟补能里程在400-500公里左右。比如智己L6光年版12分钟补能400公里，仰望U7 EV版10分钟补能503公里，理想L9 Livis版增程车型也能做到10分钟补能500公里。实际受充电桩功率和环境温度影响。

Q3：超快充车型的电池，买断和租赁怎么选？

A3：如果预算有限且计划3-5年内换车，租用电池更划算，可大幅降低首付；如果打算长期开，买断电池总成本更低、二手车残值更高。具体差价和月租需以品牌官方方案为准。

This article (published August 6, 2026, on Sina Finance) discusses the state of ultra-fast charging (超快充) technology in performance electric vehicles (EVs) in 2026. Key points include:

**Market Context:** With 5C/6C battery cells in mass production and 800V/900V high-voltage platforms becoming standard, "charging 10 minutes for hundreds of kilometers of range" has become the new normal in EVs. The 800V platform is no longer exclusive to luxury brands — entry-level 20万 (200,000 RMB) models now include it, down from the previous 40万+ threshold.

**Key Models and Pricing (from public reports by 智车星球 and 汽车之家):**
- 智己L6 (光年版): 21.99-30.59万元, 800V, 133kWh semi-solid battery, CLTC 1002km range, 12-min charge for 400km
- 小米SU7 2026: expected 22.99-30.99万元; Max version uses 897V SiC platform, 15-min charge for 670km
- 吉利银河星舰: 30-45万, 6C ultra-fast charging, 77kWh, 10-min charge for 80%
- 极氪8X: 35-50万, 900V platform, 6C charging, 1030kW, self-developed "金砖" battery
- 岚图泰山Ultra: 45.99万起, 800V 5C, 20%-80% charge in ~12 min, L3 autonomous driving
- 奔驰纯电GLC: 45-65万, 800V, 10-min charge for 300km, WLTP ~800km
- 理想L9 Livis版: 55.98万, 800V 5C, 10-min charge for 500km (range-extender)
- 尊界M900: 90-150万, 800V SiC, triple-motor 750kW, 5-min charge for 200km
- 仰望U7 EV: charge 10 minutes for 503km, with second-generation blade battery; PHEV version only adds 3 minutes charging time in -30°C conditions

**Cost Considerations:** Beyond the vehicle price, buyers must account for insurance, options, registration, charging infrastructure, and battery purchase vs. rental decisions. Battery rental (e.g., NIO's model) lowers upfront costs but may cost more long-term; purchasing is better for long-term owners due to higher resale value. Government EV subsidies (ranging from thousands to 20,000 RMB) and replacement subsidies vary by region. Home charger installation costs several thousand RMB; 480kW liquid-cooled ultra-fast charging stations are spreading but coverage remains limited in some areas.

**Battery Life and Resale:** Ultra-fast charging does not necessarily shorten battery life thanks to cell materials, thermal management, and BMS algorithms, but high-rate charging physically accelerates battery aging. Battery health will become the core pricing metric for used EVs. Most brands offer 8-year/160,000km+ battery warranties. Industry-wide battery degradation standards are still lacking.

**Practical Advice:** The industry lacks a unified definition of "ultra-fast charging" (typically 3C+ or 200km+ in 10 minutes). 5C charging requires 600kW+ chargers, so buyers should verify charging infrastructure availability before purchase. Charging speed slows significantly above 80% battery — recommended to keep charge between 20-80%. Brands with established charging networks (NIO, XPeng, 极氪) are recommended. Upcoming vehicles to watch include 蔚来ES9, 极氪8X, and 广汽埃安Hyper昊铂.

This is the official Xiaomi SU7 (second generation) product page from Xiaomi EV, showcasing the new-generation Xiaomi SU7 electric vehicle. The page covers the vehicle's design, interior, performance, range, intelligence, and safety features.

**Product Overview:**
- Starting price: 21.99万元 (219,900 RMB)
- Available in multiple trims: Standard, Pro, and Max versions
- Also promotes Xiaomi YU7 and Xiaomi SU7 Ultra models

**Exterior Design:**
- 3X wheel-to-axle ratio for aerodynamic performance and handling stability
- Water droplet headlights, halo taillights, 175° rippling curved surfaces
- Electric rear spoiler (standard on Max version)
- Available colors include Capri Blue (卡布里蓝) inspired by Italian island sea caves
- Six wheel options: 19" diamond, 20" Mi-style, 20" plum blossom, 20" blade (Standard/Pro only), 21" sport, and 21" dual-forged plum blossom wheels

**Interior Design:**
- Driver-centric axis layout with symmetrical center console
- Four interior colors: Mist Purple (迷雾紫), Sand Taupe (砂陶米), Twilight Red (暮光红), and Midnight Black (暗夜黑)
- Driver seat: 18-way adjustable sports seat with 10-point massage (standard)
- Rear seats: 20mm more padding in high-contact areas, 25mm extended seat side wings
- Standard four-door laminated quiet glass; Max version offers ultra-quiet cabin with PVB windshield
- Three-layer ambient lighting with 256 colors, synced to music and driving modes
- Max version: dual-zone smart dimming sunroof
- Speakers: 14 speakers (Standard/Pro), 25 speakers (Max)
- 105L front trunk (optional electric opening), 4.4L smart refrigerator (-6°C to 15°C cooling, 35°C-50°C heating), 29 storage compartments

**Performance:**
- Xiaomi SUPER MOTOR V6s Plus with segmented magnets and voltage over-modulation technology
- Xiaomi Jiaolong (蛟龙) chassis
- Pro/Max: closed dual-chamber air springs and CDC® dampers (20% less impact on comfort mode, up to 6.7% higher lateral acceleration on sport mode)
- All models: 265mm rear wide tires, fixed calipers (4-piston front calipers; Brembo® on Max)
- Anti-slip coordinated control system: 40% less slippage, 0.35s wheel limit slip response, 4x faster than first-gen SU7
- Wet mode upgraded with 30% better stability
